accepted.s: Recognition of political parties under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 is distinct from registration under which provision?
o: Section 19 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, 1968
Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
accepted.x: Recognition is governed by the Election Symbols Order, 1968, whereas registration of political parties is under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
accepted.tq: Separate the similar-looking concepts of registration and recognition by identifying the governing provision.
accepted.sec: National and state party recognition - criteria, number of national parties  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a valid criterion for recognition as a National Party?
o: Securing 8% of valid votes in one State
Recognition as a State Party in four or more States
Winning one Lok Sabha seat for every 25 seats allotted to a State
Recognition as a State Party in two or more States
accepted.x: Recognition as a State Party in four or more States is one of the alternative criteria for recognition as a National Party.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the national-party threshold from the nearby state-party thresholds.
accepted.sec: National and state party recognition - criteria, number of national parties  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents criteria for recognition as a State Party? 

1. Six per cent of votes in the Assembly election and two seats
2. Six per cent of votes in the Lok Sabha election and one Lok Sabha seat
3. Three per cent of Assembly seats or three seats, whichever is more
4. Eight per cent of valid votes

Select the correct answer:
accepted.x: All four listed conditions are alternative criteria for recognition as a State Party, including the Assembly, Lok Sabha, seat-share and 8% vote conditions.
accepted.tq: Check each alternative threshold independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: National and state party recognition - criteria, number of national parties  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Model Code of Conduct:

1. It is a set of guidelines issued by the Election Commission for political parties, candidates and the ruling government.
2. It is a statutory law enacted by Parliament.
3. Its authority is associated with the plenary power of the Election Commission under Article 324.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Model Code is a set of ECI guidelines and is supported by the Commission's plenary power under Article 324. It is not a statutory law enacted by Parliament.
accepted.tq: Spot the wrong legal-status statement while retaining the correct authority-based statements.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following milestones relating to the Model Code of Conduct in chronological order:

A. Part VII relating to the party in power was added
B. The Code was first drafted by the Kerala Government
C. The Code was revised
D. The Code was formalised by the Election Commission

Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: The sequence is 1960 drafting by Kerala, 1968 formalisation by the ECI, 1974 revision, and 1979 addition of Part VII.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest milestones first, then place the 1968 and 1974 events.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Model Code of Conduct was first used in which election?
accepted.x: The Model Code of Conduct was first used in the 1960 Kerala Assembly election.
accepted.tq: Distinguish first use from later formalisation and revision dates.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who enforced the Model Code of Conduct with particular strictness in 1991?
accepted.x: Chief Election Commissioner T. N. Seshan enforced the Model Code of Conduct with rigour in 1991.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to distinguish election officials and judges.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the ruling in Harbans Singh Jalal v Union of India, the Model Code of Conduct comes into force:
o: On the date of publication of election results
On announcement of the election schedule
accepted.x: The Punjab and Haryana High Court held in 1997 that the Model Code comes into force when the election schedule is announced.
accepted.tq: Identify the operative trigger instead of confusing it with nomination, polling or result dates.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a restriction under Part VII of the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Introducing new schemes or grants after announcement of polls
Using official machinery or transport for campaigning
Continuing ordinary official visits without combining them with electioneering
accepted.x: Part VII restricts combining official visits with electioneering, using official machinery or transport for campaigning, and introducing new schemes or grants after polls are announced.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not describe a prohibited act under the specific part of the Code.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Part VII of the Model Code of Conduct primarily governs the conduct of:
o: Candidates who have lost the election
accepted.x: Part VII, added in 1979, contains provisions concerning the party in power and the use of governmental machinery during elections.
accepted.tq: Link a named part of the Code with its specific institutional subject.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following may be imposed for violation of the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Dissolution of Parliament by the Chief Election Commissioner
Censure and, in serious cases, suspension or withdrawal of recognition under Paragraph 16A
Cancellation of the Constitution by the President
Automatic imprisonment by the Election Commission
accepted.x: The Election Commission may censure a party and may suspend or withdraw recognition under Paragraph 16A of the Symbols Order in appropriate cases.
accepted.tq: Ask who can impose which sanction and reject powers that belong to no election authority.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Model Code of Conduct, consider the following statements:

1. It was formalised by the Election Commission in 1968.
2. Part VII was added in 1979.
3. It is lifted immediately when polling ends, even before declaration of results.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Code is lifted once results are declared, not immediately when polling ends.
accepted.tq: Use the time-word trap in statement 3 while verifying the two historical milestones.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Model Code of Conduct was lifted in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry on 7 May 2026, except in respect of:
accepted.x: The Code was lifted in the listed jurisdictions on 7 May 2026, except for the Falta re-poll seat.
accepted.tq: Use precise exception-based recall for a date-linked administrative action.
accepted.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 326, the right to vote in elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies is based on:
accepted.x: Article 326 provides for elections based on universal adult suffrage, with the voting age being 18 years.
accepted.tq: Separate the constitutional voting principle from outdated age and qualification conditions.
accepted.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal nature of the right to vote in India?
o: It is a statutory right under the Representation of the People Acts
It is a constitutional right enforceable only through Article 32
It is an absolute natural right outside the Constitution and statutes
It is a Fundamental Right under Article 19
accepted.x: The right to vote is a statutory right under the Representation of the People Acts and is not a Fundamental Right.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among constitutional, fundamental and statutory rights using the exact legal classification.
accepted.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

accepted.s: A citizen who is disqualified on grounds of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice is:
o: Entitled to vote only in Rajya Sabha elections
Excluded from the right to vote under the qualifications and disqualifications governing Article 326
Entitled to vote if the person deposits a security amount
Automatically entitled to vote under Article 326
accepted.x: Article 326 permits voting by citizens aged 18 or above subject to disqualifications such as non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime and corrupt or illegal practice.
accepted.tq: Apply the general rule to a fact pattern by checking the stated statutory disqualifications.
accepted.sec: Universal adult franchise - Article 326, voting age  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the first-past-the-post system used for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections?
o: The candidate is elected only after securing more than half of the valid votes.
Seats are distributed strictly in proportion to the total votes polled by each party.
The candidate securing a majority of all registered voters wins.
The candidate securing the highest number of votes in a single-member constituency wins.
accepted.x: Under the territorial single-member first-past-the-post system, the candidate with the highest plurality of votes wins; an absolute majority is not required.
accepted.tq: Distinguish plurality from majority and proportional representation.
accepted.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Proportional representation through the single transferable vote is used for elections to which of the following?

1. Rajya Sabha
2. Legislative Councils
3. President and Vice-President
4. Lok Sabha

Select the correct answer:
accepted.x: Single transferable vote-based proportional representation is used for the Rajya Sabha, Legislative Councils, President and Vice-President. Lok Sabha elections use first-past-the-post.
accepted.tq: Separate the institutions using proportional representation from those using territorial first-past-the-post.
accepted.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a reason for rejecting proportional representation for Lok Sabha elections?
o: It may encourage fragmentation and unstable governments.
It guarantees a direct election in every single-member constituency.
It weakens the voter–Member of Parliament link.
It may be difficult for voters to understand.
accepted.x: Difficulty for voters, fragmentation, unstable governments, expense, absence of by-elections and a weaker voter–MP link are cited concerns. Guaranteeing direct election in every single-member constituency is not such a reason.
accepted.tq: Find the option that is outside the stated list of objections to proportional representation.
accepted.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

accepted.s: A candidate's security deposit is forfeited when the candidate secures less than:
accepted.x: The security deposit is forfeited if the candidate obtains less than one-sixth of the valid votes.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact fractional threshold and distinguish it from common one-fourth and one-third distractors.
accepted.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court directed the inclusion of a NOTA option on all Electronic Voting Machines in:
o: Harbans Singh Jalal v Union of India, 1997
Mohinder Singh Gill v Chief Election Commissioner, 1978
Kuldip Nayar v Union of India, 2006
accepted.x: In PUCL v Union of India on 27 September 2013, the Supreme Court directed that a NOTA button be provided on all EVMs.
accepted.tq: Match the election-related judicial direction with the correct case and year.
accepted.sec: NOTA - PUCL case, year, effect on result

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the electoral effect of NOTA?
o: NOTA votes are transferred to the candidate placed second.
Even if NOTA receives the highest number of votes, the candidate with the highest votes among the contesting candidates is declared elected.
The election is automatically cancelled if NOTA receives the highest votes.
A re-poll is compulsory whenever NOTA exceeds the winning candidate's votes.
accepted.x: NOTA has no electoral effect on the result. Even when NOTA receives the most votes, the highest-scoring contesting candidate wins.
accepted.tq: Apply the no-electoral-effect rule to a hypothetical result scenario.
accepted.sec: NOTA - PUCL case, year, effect on result

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the NOTA symbol and its first Lok Sabha use is correct?
o: It is a blank ballot, designed by the Supreme Court, and was first used in 2013.
It is a ballot with a black cross, designed by Parliament, and was first used in 2024.
It is a ballot with a black cross, designed by NID Ahmedabad, and was first used in 2014.
It is a ballot with a red star, designed by the Election Commission, and was first used in 2019.
accepted.x: The NOTA symbol is a ballot with a black cross, designed by the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad; it was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014.
accepted.tq: Combine symbol, designing institution and first-use year without confusing the judicial-order year with the implementation year.
accepted.sec: NOTA - PUCL case, year, effect on result

accepted.s: The first general election to the Lok Sabha in India was held in:
accepted.x: India's first general election was held in 1951–52.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first election period from the year in which the First Lok Sabha was constituted.
accepted.sec: Lok Sabha general elections - number, Lok Sabha to year, FIRST election  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The 18th Lok Sabha was elected in which year?
accepted.x: The 18th Lok Sabha was elected in 2024; the 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019.
accepted.tq: Separate consecutive Lok Sabha numbers from their corresponding election years.
accepted.sec: Lok Sabha general elections - number, Lok Sabha to year, FIRST election  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match the following Lok Sabhas with the years of their election.

List-I
(a) 1st Lok Sabha
(b) 9th Lok Sabha
(c) 11th Lok Sabha
(d) 16th Lok Sabha

List-II
(i) 1996
(ii) 1952
(iii) 2014
(iv) 1989

Select the correct answer using the code below:
accepted.x: The 1st, 9th, 11th and 16th Lok Sabhas correspond respectively to 1952, 1989, 1996 and 2014.
accepted.tq: Start with the fixed 1st Lok Sabha–1952 pair and eliminate codes around it.
accepted.sec: Lok Sabha general elections - number, Lok Sabha to year, FIRST election  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the total number of Lok Sabha general elections held so far and the election year of the 17th Lok Sabha?
accepted.x: There have been 18 Lok Sabha general elections so far, and the 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019; the 18th was elected in 2024.
accepted.tq: Keep the total count separate from the year of the immediately preceding Lok Sabha.
